title: Item categories and a category filter on the list
body:
Each item now has a category, and the list page can be filtered to one category. ## What you should know - **Behaviour change:** `/` shows each item's category and has "All" plus one link per category. `/?category=` lists only that category. An unknown, empty or repeated `category` answers 404 with "This link seems to be corrupted." and a "Go back" link. - **Decisions:** categories have their own table with unique, non-empty names, and `items.category_id` is nullable so the previous app version keeps working. Names match exactly, case-sensitive. "Go back" goes back only to a page of this app and otherwise goes to `/`. Synthetic traffic now also requests `/?category=Work`. All of these are in `specs/item-categories.md`. - **Tests deleted or loosened:** none. The `
  • First item
    • ` assertion is now the AC-3 markup, as the spec says. The traffic config check now accepts a query string in a route (AC-11) and still rejects whitespace, `#` and paths without a leading `/`; new cases cover whitespace and `#`. - **Manual steps for you:** none. The migration runs in the deploy before the new code goes live.
    Engineering details - `migrations/0003_item_categories.sql` creates `categories(id, name NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (name <> ''))`, adds the nullable `items.category_id REFERENCES categories(id)` with the index `items_category_id`, and seeds Work and Home, tagging the three seeded items by title. It is additive only: old-style inserts get a null category. - `src/index.js` reads the category list, matches `URLSearchParams.getAll("category")` against it, and lists items in `id` order. Names are URL-encoded in links and HTML-escaped in text. The broken-link page is a 404 with a plain `href="/"`, plus a small inline script that calls `history.back()` only when the referrer is same-origin. - `test/apply-migrations.js` drops tables in one batch with `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON`, so drop order no longer matters (AC-13). - `scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs` allows `?` in a route. `test/traffic.test.js`'s fake app records path plus query.
